notesStmt.note: The notes in Whitman's hand in blue pencil, including the number in the top right, are similar to those that appear on other manuscripts and seem to indicate that this manuscript was used as the copy-text for the printing of November Boughs. According to Horace Traubel, Whitman sent the copy for the poetry section of November Boughs to the printer on June 1, 1888, so Whitman's note on this proof were made before that date, likely in early 1888.
A proof slip of "Yonnondio," which was first published in the Critic on November 26, 1887. The poem was later reprinted in November Boughs (1888).

lg.head: YONNONDIO.
lg.note:
[The sense of the word is lament for the aborigines. It is an Iroquois term;)
and has been used for a personal name.]
lg.l: A song, a poem of itself—the word itself a dirge,
Amid the wilds, the rocks, the storm and wintry night;
To me such misty, strange tableaux the syllables calling up;

Yonnondio—I see, far in the west or north, a limitless ra-
vine,ravine,
with plains and mountains dark

I see swarms of stalwart chieftains, medicine-men, and war-
riors,warriors,

As flitting by like clouds of ghosts, they pass and are gone
in the twilight,
(Race of the woods, the landscapes free, and the falls!
No picture, poem, statement, passing them to the future:)
To-day gives place, and fades—the cities, farms, factories fade;

A muffled sonorous sound, a wailing word is borne through
the air for a moment,
Then blank and gone and still, and utterly lost.
